questions.q: Glomerular filtration rate is defined as the amount of urine filtered by:
opts: All the nephrons in both kidneys in one minute
All nephrons of one kidney in one hour
The glomerular capillaries in one second
questions.exp: Definition: amount of urine filtered by all the nephrons in both kidneys in one minute. (Book p734)

questions.q: Fill up: GFR = net ultrafiltration pressure × the ultrafiltration (UF) ______.
questions.exp: GFR = net ultrafiltration pressure × ultrafiltration (UF) coefficient. (Book p734)

questions.q: Match each Starling pressure of the glomerulus with its book value — 1) Glomerular hydrostatic pressure 2) Bowman's capsule pressure 3) Glomerular colloid osmotic pressure … A) 32 mm Hg B) 60 mm Hg C) 18 mm Hg
questions.exp: Glomerular hydrostatic 60 mm Hg; Bowman's capsule 18 mm Hg; glomerular colloid osmotic 32 mm Hg. (Book p734)

questions.q: The net filtration pressure worked out in the book's boxes is:
questions.exp: Net filtration pressure (10 mm Hg) = glomerular hydrostatic (60) − Bowman's capsule (18) − glomerular oncotic (32). (Book p734)

questions.q: Using [(60 − 18) − (32 − 0)] × 12.5 ml/min/mmHg, the book's calculated GFR is:
questions.exp: = 10 × 12.5 ml/min = 125 ml/min. (Book p734)

questions.q: Fill up: In the expansion of the oncotic term, the Bowman's space oncotic pressure is taken as ______.
questions.exp: (Glomerular capillary OP − Bowman's space OP) uses Bowman's space OP = 0. (Book p734)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the GFR calculation is TRUE?
opts: Net ultrafiltration pressure = net hydrostatic pressure minus net oncotic pressure
Net ultrafiltration pressure = net oncotic pressure minus net hydrostatic pressure
The UF coefficient is subtracted from the net pressure
Bowman's capsule pressure adds to filtration
questions.exp: GFR = [net hydrostatic pressure (H.P) − net oncotic pressure (O.P)] × UF coefficient. (Book p734)

questions.q: Normal GFR as written in the book is:
questions.exp: Normal GFR: 90–125 ml/min. (Book p734)

questions.q: The principal use of GFR listed is that:
opts: Chronic kidney disease is classified based on GFR
questions.exp: Use: chronic kidney disease (CKD) is classified based on GFR. (Book p734)

questions.q: Fill up: A GFR below 15 ml/min marks G5 / end-stage renal disease / the uremic phase, when ______ is required.
questions.exp: Eg: GFR <15 ml/min: G5/ESRD/uremic phase (dialysis required). (Book p734)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about GFR staging is TRUE?
opts: GFR <15 ml/min corresponds to G5/ESRD, the uremic phase needing dialysis
GFR <15 ml/min corresponds to G2 CKD
GFR <15 ml/min needs no replacement therapy
questions.exp: GFR <15 ml/min = G5/ESRD/uremic phase, dialysis required. (Book p734)

questions.q: The best marker to estimate GFR is:
questions.exp: Creatinine: best marker to estimate GFR. (Book p735)

questions.q: Fill up: Creatinine is produced in muscle from ______.
questions.exp: Produced in muscle from creatine; ↓ when muscle mass is reduced (eg: amputation). (Book p735)

questions.q: Serum creatinine falls when muscle mass is reduced; the book's example is:
questions.exp: ↓ sed when muscle mass reduced (eg: amputation). (Book p735)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about creatinine in pregnancy is TRUE?
opts: Pregnancy is the only condition where high creatinine values are significant independently
Creatinine values lose all significance in pregnancy
Pregnancy raises the normal creatinine range to 1.5–2 mg/dL
Creatinine cannot be measured in pregnancy
questions.exp: Pregnancy: only condition where high creatinine values are significant independently (normal 0.3–0.6 mg/dL). (Book p735)

questions.q: The normal creatinine range quoted for pregnancy is:
questions.exp: Normal in pregnancy: 0.3–0.6 mg/dL. (Book p735)

questions.q: Creatinine is described as a molecule of:
questions.exp: Creatinine = 113 kDa molecule (cystatin C is the 13 kDa protein). (Book p735)

questions.q: The Cockcroft & Gault equation is labelled in the book as:
opts: The only bedside formula still preferred
questions.exp: Cockcroft & Gault equation: obsolete; not preferred now due to disadvantages (though it is a bed-side formula). (Book p735)

questions.q: Fill up: In the Cockcroft & Gault creatinine clearance, the female result is the male formula multiplied by ______.
questions.exp: CrCl = (140−age) × BW / (72 × S.Cr) in males; × 0.8 in females. (Book p735)

questions.q: The denominator constant of the Cockcroft & Gault equation is:
questions.exp: Denominator: 72 × S.creatinine. (Book p735)

questions.q: Match each GFR equation with its origin — 1) MDRD equation 2) CKD-EPI equation 3) Schwartz equation … A) CKD-Epidemiology problem initiative group; best when GFR > 60 B) Society for modification of diet & renal diseases C) Estimates GFR in children
questions.exp: MDRD = society for modification of diet & renal diseases; CKD-EPI = CKD-Epidemiology problem initiative group (best when GFR > 60); Schwartz = children. (Book p735)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about GFR equations is TRUE?
opts: MDRD and CKD-EPI are the preferred equations now
Cockcroft & Gault is the preferred equation now
Schwartz equation is used in adults only
questions.exp: MDRD and CKD-EPI are bracketed as 'preferred now'; CKD-EPI is best (advantage when GFR > 60). (Book p735)

questions.q: All of the following are disadvantages of the Cockcroft & Gault equation EXCEPT:
opts: It uses race instead of weight
It overestimates GFR by assuming CrCl = GFR
Creatinine secretion makes CrCl = GFR + tubular secretion
It was developed when Cr was estimated by Jaffe's alkaline-picrate method
questions.exp: Using race instead of weight is an advantage of MDRD/CKD-EPI; C&G over-emphasises BW, overestimates GFR and rests on Jaffe's method. (Book p735)

questions.q: Fill up: The MDRD/CKD-EPI equations estimate creatinine with standard assays, namely ______ (isotope dilution mass spectroscopy).
questions.exp: Advantage: equation uses estimation of Cr using standard assays: IDm (isotope dilution mass spectroscopy). (Book p735)

questions.q: Because creatinine is secreted, the book writes creatinine clearance as:
opts: GFR + tubular secretion (or GFR − tubular absorption)
questions.exp: Cr is secreted → CrCl = GFR + tubular secretion (clearance = GFR + tubular secretion or GFR − tubular absorption). (Book p735)

questions.q: In the Schwartz equation, the constant K for a term infant under 1 year (age not mentioned) is:
questions.exp: <1 yr: pre-term 0.33, term 0.45 (if age not mentioned). (Book p736)

questions.q: Match each child group with its Schwartz constant K — 1) Pre-term <1 yr 2) Term <1 yr 3) 1–2 yr and adolescent girls 4) Adolescent boys … A) 0.45 B) 0.33 C) 0.7 D) 0.55
questions.exp: K: pre-term 0.33; term 0.45; 1–2 yr & adolescent girls 0.55; adolescent boys 0.7. (Book p736)

questions.q: Fill up: The Schwartz equation computes eGFR as K × the child's ______ divided by S.Cr.
questions.exp: eGFR = K × length of child / S.Cr. (Book p736)

questions.q: In acute kidney injury, creatinine takes how long to start rising?
questions.exp: Disadvantage 1: 24–48 hrs to start rising in AKI. (Book p736)

questions.q: Creatinine is dependent on all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Dependent on muscle mass, race, age and sex; obesity causes no change in S.Cr as fat doesn't affect S.Cr. (Book p736)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about creatinine determinants is TRUE as written in the book?
opts: Creatinine is lower in African Americans
Creatinine is higher in African Americans
Creatinine rises after 40 years of age
Creatinine is independent of muscle mass
questions.exp: Determinants as written: muscle mass (↓ muscle mass → ↓ Cr), race (↓ in African Americans), age (↓ after 40 years d/t ↓ muscle mass) and sex (↓ in males). (Book p736)

questions.q: Fill up: Creatinine falls after 40 years of age because of the decline in ______.
questions.exp: Age (↓ after 40 years d/t ↓ in muscle mass). (Book p736)

questions.q: Fill up: In obesity there is no change in S.Cr because ______ does not affect S.Cr.
questions.exp: Obesity: no change in S.Cr as fat doesn't affect S.Cr. (Book p736)

questions.q: Fill up: Cimetidine and trimethoprim raise serum creatinine by competing with Cr for tubular ______.
questions.exp: They compete with Cr for tubular secretion → ↓ tubular secretion of Cr → ↑ serum Cr. (Book p736)

questions.q: On the inverse-relationship graph, by the time S.Cr reaches 2 mg/dL the GFR has fallen to about:
questions.exp: By the time S.Cr = 2, GFR falls to ~60 ml/min. (Book p736)

questions.q: A patient's serum creatinine rises from 1.7 to 2.8 mg/dL. Per the book's inverse-relationship examples, this rise means the GFR has:
opts: Fallen insignificantly because the patient was already in ESRD
questions.exp: ↑ in S.Cr from 1.7 to 2.8: GFR falls significantly (50 ml/min → 30 ml/min); the 5→20 example is the insignificant one (already ESRD). (Book p736)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the GFR–creatinine relationship is TRUE?
opts: By the time creatinine rises, GFR has already fallen significantly
Creatinine rises before any fall in GFR
An initial creatinine rise corresponds to a trivial GFR fall
questions.exp: Inverse relationship: by the time Cr rises GFR falls significantly; the initial rise in Cr corresponds to a significant fall in GFR. (Book p736)

questions.q: Fill up: Whole-kidney GFR equals single nephron GFR multiplied by the ______ of nephrons.
questions.exp: GFR = single nephron GFR × number of nephrons. (Book p737)

questions.q: Which sequence matches the book's hyperfiltration-injury note?
opts: ↓ nephron number → ↑ snGFR to maintain GFR → beyond compensation intraglomerular HTN → proteinuria → interstitial fibrosis → ↓ GFR
questions.exp: Even if number ↓, snGFR ↑ to maintain GFR (hyperfiltration injury); beyond the point of compensation: intraglomerular HTN → proteinuria → interstitial fibrosis → ↓ GFR. (Book p737)

questions.q: Fill up: Clearance equals urine concentration × urine volume (V) divided by the ______ concentration.
questions.exp: Clearance = (urine concentration × volume of urine in ml/min (V)) / plasma concentration. (Book p737)

questions.q: Endogenous creatinine clearance is written as:
questions.exp: Endogenous Cr clearance = U_cr × V / P_cr. (Book p737)

questions.q: Match each cystatin C fact with its descriptor — 1) Size 2) Biochemical class 3) Production … A) Constant rate by all nucleated cells B) 13 kDa molecule protein C) Cysteine protease inhibitor
questions.exp: Cystatin C: 13 kDa molecule protein; cysteine protease inhibitor; produced at constant rate by all nucleated cells. (Book p737)

questions.q: All of the following describe cystatin C handling EXCEPT:
opts: It is secreted by the PCT
It is filtered but not secreted
It is reabsorbed by the PCT
It is produced at a constant rate
questions.exp: Cystatin C: filtered but not secreted; reabsorbed by PCT; constant production — it is never secreted. (Book p737)

questions.q: Cystatin C is not affected by all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Advantages: not affected by race, diet, muscle mass or drugs; inflammation (with steroids and smoking) elevates it non-specifically. (Book p737)

questions.q: Fill up: Because of its non-specific elevations, cystatin C cannot replace ______.
questions.exp: Therefore, cannot replace Cr. (Book p737)

questions.q: Cystatin C is non-specifically elevated in inflammation, smokers and patients:
questions.exp: Non specifically elevated in: inflammation, taking steroids, smokers. (Book p737)

questions.q: The renal autoregulation range of mean arterial pressure is:
questions.exp: Within auto regulation range (MAP: 80–180 mmHg); 40–240 is only the graph axis. (Book p738)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about renal autoregulation is TRUE?
opts: Within the autoregulation range RBF and GFR are constant
Within the range RBF rises linearly with pressure
GFR falls to zero within the range
questions.exp: Renal blood flow (RBF) and GFR are constant within the autoregulation range. (Book p738)

questions.q: Match each autoregulation mechanism with its descriptor — 1) Myogenic reflex 2) Tubulo glomerular feedback … A) Adenosine mediated B) Stretch reflex
questions.exp: Mechanisms: myogenic reflex (stretch reflex) and tubulo glomerular feedback (adenosine mediated). (Book p738)

questions.q: Fill up: In response to a falling GFR (eg: pre-renal failure), the afferent arteriole undergoes ______, raising filtration.
questions.exp: In response to ↓ GFR → afferent arteriolar vasodilatation → ↑ filtration. (Book p738)

questions.q: Fill up: With ↑ GFR/tubular injury, more NaCl/KCl reaches the macula densa and releases ______, causing afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction.
questions.exp: ↑ NaCl/KCl reach macula densa → adenosine → afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction → ↓ filtration. (Book p738)

questions.q: In the glomerulo-tubular balance example at GFR = 200 ml/min, the amounts reabsorbed and excreted are:
questions.exp: GFR 200: Na+ filtered 200 meq → 198 meq reabsorbed, 2 meq excreted (1%). (Book p738)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about glomerulo-tubular balance is TRUE?
opts: The percentage of Na+ excreted remains constant as reabsorption compensates
The percentage of Na+ excreted doubles when GFR doubles
Reabsorption stays fixed while excretion rises
questions.exp: ↑ GFR → ↑ reabsorption by tubule (compensation) → % of Na+ excreted remains constant (1% in both examples). (Book p738)

questions.q: Fill up: Renal plasma flow (700 ml) is estimated using para amino hippuric acid, abbreviated ______.
questions.exp: RPF = 700 ml: estimated using para amino hippuric acid (PAH). (Book p738)

questions.q: The filtration fraction computed as 125/700 equals:
Fill up: A raised filtration fraction increases peritubular capillary oncotic pressure, taking fluid from the interstitial space and lowering renal interstitial ______, which boosts PCT reabsorption.
questions.exp: ↑ FF → ↑ peritubular capillary OP → taken-in fluid from interstitial space → ↓ renal interstitial HP (RIHP) → ↑ reabsorption from PCT. (Book p738)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about pressure natriuresis is TRUE?
opts: A raised cardiac output increases excretion of Na+ and H2O
A raised cardiac output decreases sodium excretion
questions.exp: ↑ CO leads to ↑ excretion of Na+ & H2O; therefore ↑ CO cannot produce sustained ↑ BP unless there is renal impairment. (Book p738)

questions.q: The book's pressure-natriuresis caveat uses which blood-pressure identity?
questions.exp: Therefore, ↑ CO cannot produce sustained ↑ in BP unless there is renal impairment (BP = CO × PVR). (Book p738)

questions.q: Match each step of the pressure-natriuresis mechanism with what follows — 1) ↑ CO 2) ↓ Reabsorption from PCT 3) ↑ Medullary blood flow … A) ↑ Na+ & H2O excretion B) ↑ RBF C) ↑ RIHP
questions.exp: ↑ CO → ↑ RBF → ↓ reabsorption from PCT → ↑ RIHP → ↑ medullary blood flow → ↑ Na+ & H2O excretion. (Book p739)

questions.q: Fill up: Afferent arteriolar dilatation in the hemodynamics list is mediated by ______.
questions.exp: Afferent arteriolar dilatation (mediated by prostaglandins). (Book p739)

questions.q: Fill up: Efferent arteriolar constriction in the hemodynamics list is mediated by ______.
questions.exp: Efferent arteriolar constriction (mediated by angiotensin II). (Book p739)

questions.q: Match each arteriolar resistance change with its renal-blood-flow and net-ultrafiltration-pressure pair — 1) Increased afferent 2) Decreased afferent 3) Increased efferent 4) Decreased efferent … A) RBF ↑, NUP ↑ (favourable for kidney) B) RBF ↓, NUP ↓ (unfavourable) C) RBF ↓, NUP ↑ (unfavourable) D) RBF ↑, NUP ↓ (unfavourable)
questions.exp: Table: increased afferent ↓↓; decreased afferent ↑↑ (favourable); increased efferent ↓↑; decreased efferent ↑↓ — all but decreased afferent are unfavourable. (Book p739)

questions.q: Efferent arteriolar constriction reduces blood flow to the medulla and causes:
questions.exp: Efferent arteriolar constriction → ↓ blood flow to medulla → medullary hypoxia. (Book p739)

questions.q: In the normal-blood-flow note, the sequence after the efferent arteriole is:
opts: Peritubular capillary → vasa recta → renal medulla
Vasa recta → peritubular capillary → renal cortex
Peritubular capillary → renal pelvis → vasa recta
Glomerular capillary → vasa recta → peritubular capillary
questions.exp: Efferent arteriole → peritubular capillary → vasa recta → renal medulla. (Book p739)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about ACE inhibitors is TRUE per the book?
opts: Blocking angiotensin II dilates the efferent arteriole, lowering GFR (↑S.Cr) but raising blood flow
ACE inhibitors constrict the efferent arteriole
ACE inhibitors raise GFR by dilating the afferent arteriole
ACE inhibitors are harmful in all nephrology patients
questions.exp: ACE inhibitor: block angiotensin II → efferent arteriolar dilatation → ↓ GFR (↑S.Cr) but ↑ blood flow; beneficial for nephrology patients. (Book p739)

questions.q: A patient with bilateral renal artery stenosis is started on an ACE inhibitor and deteriorates. The book's explanation is that:
opts: The afferent arteriole is not working and the efferent arteriole was maintaining GFR
The efferent arteriole was already fully dilated
Prostaglandins were blocking the afferent arteriole
questions.exp: C/I in patients with b/l renal artery stenosis: afferent arteriole not working, efferent arteriole maintains GFR — removing angiotensin II collapses that support. (Book p739)

questions.q: Fill up: NSAIDs block prostaglandins and thereby block ______ arteriolar dilatation, leaving efferent constriction to lower GFR and RBF.
questions.exp: NSAID: block prostaglandins → block afferent arteriolar dilatation → efferent arteriolar constriction → ↓ GFR & ↓ RBF. (Book p739)

questions.q: NSAIDs are contraindicated in patients already on ACE inhibitors because blocking angiotensin II removes efferent constriction and precipitates:
questions.exp: C/I in patients on ACE(−): ACEI → efferent arteriolar constriction blocked → frank renal failure. (Book p739)

questions.q: All of the following are listed arteriolar events in the glomerular-hemodynamics section EXCEPT:
opts: Afferent arteriolar constriction mediated by angiotensin II
Afferent arteriolar dilatation mediated by prostaglandins
Efferent arteriolar constriction mediated by angiotensin II
questions.exp: The book pairs afferent dilatation with prostaglandins and efferent constriction with angiotensin II; afferent constriction carries no angiotensin-II label. (Book p739)

units.title: GFR: definition & Starling calculation

units.title: Normal GFR & its clinical use
units.guide: Normal range 90–125 ml/min, CKD classification by GFR and the G5/ESRD uremic phase below 15 ml/min needing dialysis.

units.title: Creatinine as the GFR marker
units.guide: Creatinine basics: best marker, muscle creatine source, muscle-mass dependence, the pregnancy exception with its 0.3–0.6 mg/dL normal, and the 113 kDa size.

units.title: GFR equations: C&G, MDRD, CKD-EPI, Schwartz
units.guide: The obsolete Cockcroft & Gault formula (×0.8 in females, 72 denominator) versus preferred MDRD/CKD-EPI (IDm assays, race), the disadvantages table, and Schwartz K constants for children.

units.title: Disadvantages of creatinine & the inverse curve
units.guide: 24–48 h lag in AKI, muscle/race/age/sex dependence, diet and obesity effects, cimetidine/trimethoprim competition, and the inverse GFR–creatinine curve with its 1.7→2.8 and 5→20 examples.

units.title: snGFR note, clearance formula & cystatin C
units.guide: GFR = snGFR × nephron number with the hyperfiltration-injury chain, the U×V/P clearance formula, and cystatin C's properties, advantages and non-specific elevations.

units.title: Autoregulation & glomerulo-tubular balance
units.guide: The 80–180 mmHg autoregulation range, myogenic reflex and adenosine-mediated TGF with their afferent responses, and GT balance keeping excreted Na+ at 1%.

units.title: Filtration fraction & pressure natriuresis
units.guide: FF = GFR/RPF with PAH-estimated 700 ml (0.1–0.2), the peritubular-oncotic/RIHP consequence, and the pressure-natriuresis theory with its CO→RBF→RIHP→medullary-flow mechanism.

units.title: Glomerular hemodynamics & ACEI/NSAID notes
units.guide: Prostaglandin/angiotensin-II mediation of arteriolar changes, the favourable-vs-unfavourable resistance table, medullary hypoxia, and the ACE-inhibitor and NSAID contraindication chains.
